body: Shouldn't this use `get_viewport()->gui_get_drag_data()`? Otherwise the control is checking data from itself.

Well the question is valid , but the gui_get_drag_data() is global function and it returns the true raw variant , but in the scene tree editor or other dock tree control, 
the get_drag_data() is overrided to check if the global data can be converted into my tree system , so I have to get the local data after the override to check if the drop is valid for the tree control itself  and then scroll should be allowed. Thanks for the feedback. Is my reasoning wrong? I can make the required changes if it's wrong.@KoBeWi

`get_drag_data()`, as it is used here, will return drag data from _this_ control. So `can_drop_data()` is checking whether _this_ Tree can accept data from that same Tree. That feels redundant.

I tested whether it works, and it seemingly does for the most part, but dragging a Node from Scene dock will no longer scroll FileSystem dock. However switching to `gui_get_drag_data()` does not fix it :/

You want node from scene manager to be able to scroll filesystem but not the opposite right, and the ui dock button should not scroll anything. Or something else is desired . OK, I will see into it once more. Thanks for the feedback. @KoBeWi
Yes, you can drag and drop from Scene to FileSystem, but not the opposite (at least currently).

So I know I said that dropping from FileSystem to Scene dock is not supported, but I realized I forgot that you can drop files onto nodes .-. You can assign e.g. textures to a sprite this way. This change breaks it.

Given how much trouble this fix causes, I think the best solution would be just hard-code an exception when dragging a tab. In the end the original issue is that docks get scrolled when you are dragging them.

You can check whether drag data has "type" set to "tab" to achieve it.
